notes: Implemented the wedge non-degeneracy checker (BG-INV-109, v1: midpoint sampling) per decisions 1-5: build the edge->face-uses map from `face.boundary_iters()`; for each edge with exactly two uses (open boundaries and >2 uses skipped), sample the curve's parameter midpoint, project it onto both faces' surfaces via `search_parameter` (a failed projection or an unbounded parameter range is `NumericallyUnresolved`/`UncertifiedContainment`, never a violation), take the unit normals and require `|n_A x n_B| >= sin_margin`. Holds certificate is the house structural shape with `Method::Float` (the sampling is f64 arithmetic) and `Prop::WedgeNonDegeneracy = True`; the violation is the verbatim `Contradictory { prop: WedgeNonDegeneracy, left: True, right: False }`. The offending edge is the first in `edge_iter` order whose check fails (each distinct edge tested once via a HashSet of seen ids). Added the five required unit tests (right-angle 90-degree tent holds with sin margin 0.5; folded coplanar faces violate; doubled-back faces with reversed surface normal violate; single-face shell with only boundary edges is Ok; plane translated off the shared edge is NumericallyUnresolved) plus the right-angle-tent `is_ok()` doctest on check. Note on the doubled-back witness: the checker samples the geometric surface normal (`face.surface().normal(u,v)`), not the wire orientation, so the antiparallel normals are encoded via opposite surface orientation (Plane with swapped u/v points) while B's wire traverses the shared edge in the same sense as A's, per the packet's description.
